prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation remains the clearest case on the shortlist of a single physical principle with large generative potential: a small molecule induces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, and occupancy-based inhibition becomes event-driven, catalytic removal. The ternary-complex cooperativity and turnover are quantitative, and the mechanism has been reproduced independently across many laboratories and target classes. Seven of eight members place B056 in their preferred configuration, and the first round showed that the disagreement is about one seat, not about the science. I now put the third seat with Handa. Each of the three names then rests on a distinct, datable step: the PROTAC concept and first proof of principle (Crews, Deshaies, 2001) and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide (Handa), which gives the molecular-glue strand a mechanistic origin and explains the CRBN-recruiting degraders that dominate the clinic. The citation can be explained to a broad audience as recruiting ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, and it covers both strands without needing to name every contributor.
statement.case_against: The three-name limit leaves out people with real claims: Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex design), Sakamoto (co-author of the 2001 paper), Ito (cereblon with Handa), Gray and Kim. The PROTAC and glue lineages arose somewhat independently, so a combined citation can be read as a compromise between two discoveries. No degrader is yet a broadly established approved therapy, so part of the case for impact is prospective, and I am recalling trial status, not verifying it. Somfai also asks how much is chemically new beyond ligand and linker optimisation, and the expert report should address that directly.

responses.point: Brzezinski argues that Crews-Deshaies-Handa is the cleanest attribution because each name rests on a distinct, datable discovery, whereas Ciulli's VHL and ternary-complex work reads as a strong line of work and not a single attributable discovery.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me. In round 1 I asked every member to separate the original discovery from later refinement, and by that test the cereblon identification is a founding step, while the VHL ligand and cooperativity work, however important for quantitative design, refines and generalises a concept that Crews and Deshaies had already shown. I accept your boundary and drop Ciulli from my three names. I share your worry that naming Handa could read as awarding two discoveries, so I want the expert report to state clearly how much of the ternary-complex framework belongs to Ciulli and how much to the Crews laboratory, and I want the citation worded around the shared principle of recruiting ubiquitin ligases.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, with cereblon anchoring the molecular-glue branch, and says a unified citation can cover the PROTAC concept and the thalidomide-type glues under one principle.
responses.response: In round 1 I said I could be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive original step, and your argument that thalidomide-type glues underlie most CRBN-recruiting degraders in the clinic, together with the datable nature of Handa's result, does that. I have adopted your configuration and a citation close to yours. I still think the citation must rest on the principle of recruiting ligases to remove chosen proteins and not on clinical outcomes, because no degrader is yet broadly approved and that argument should not depend on trial results neither of us has verified. I would also keep Ito and Sakamoto explicit in the expert report as recognised contributors, so that the leaving-out is documented and not silent.

responses.point: Sparr argues that waiting for an approved degrader would hold the prize hostage to regulatory events, that twenty-five years of independent reproduction is the relevant maturity, and that Ciulli's biophysical work is what made degraders quantitatively understood.
responses.response: I agree on maturity: the criterion should be independent reproduction of a mechanism that is quantitatively understood, and that is met after twenty-five years, with or without a first approval. On Ciulli, I still value the biophysics, since cooperativity is exactly the quantitative evidence I look for, but I now regard it as the deepening of a discovery and not the founding step, which is why I moved to Handa. I recognise this displaces the trio you and Zou prefer. If you can name a dated Ciulli result that opened a capability not already shown by the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism, I would listen, but absent that I ask you to weigh the glue strand being left unrecognised against Ciulli being left out.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B051) with Buchwald and Hartwig as a mature, general method with a clean two-person split, and says he would move toward B056 if the committee wants to reward a modality instead of a method.
responses.response: I take your maturity and credit arguments seriously: B051 is the cleaner credit split on the shortlist. My difficulty is still that it extends a disconnection the committee honoured in 2010 and carries Kosugi's tin-amide precedent, so I cannot yet state what is new at the level of principle. Degraders, by contrast, change the kind of target a chemist can address. On your doubt that much of B056 is only ligand and linker optimisation, I think the new content lies in event-driven catalytic pharmacology and the cereblon mechanism, and not in the optimisation. I would welcome your view on whether a Handa-based citation answers that, since you have said you could move toward B056.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports will show cereblon (Handa, with Ito) to be the more decisive original step than the VHL and ternary-complex work, which is what my change of position depends on.
Whether a single citation can cover both lineages without looking like a compromise, given that PROTACs and glues arose largely independently.
Whether the missing approved degrader makes the prize premature for some members; I rely on recollection of trial status, not verified data.
Whether Sakamoto's or Ito's claim should displace Deshaies or Handa; I have not seen evidence that would justify this.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on B056, B048 or B068. Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues, a collegial connection and not a conflict with any candidate. As chair and a physicist I rely on the chemical-biology members for field detail and aim to run the discussion neutrally between the Handa and Ciulli positions. No change from round 1.
